purpose: Base states for the RQ2 live screening pilot (D-040). The frozen offline packet at configs/pilot-manifest.json is immutable and is NOT edited by this file.
preregistration_note: Declared before the 2026-08-28 second live run. The `signal-repair` state is deliberately constructed so that a plausible wrong answer lands in the guided-repairable class: every action type carries required preconditions and required effects, and no zero-effect or quest-stage-rollback action exists. A guided advantage measured on this state therefore demonstrates that the mechanism transfers to live proposals in a regime that contains repairable errors. It does NOT show that this regime is representative of general play, and it cannot be reported as a population effect. Executing signal-repair v1 revealed a state-design defect (missing knowledge set for the acting actor); v1 is retained as superseded and v2 is the corrected pre-registered state. The correction removes an irreparable co-occurring error; it does not change which repair strategy is being compared.

frozen-pilot-base.description: Pointer to the immutable offline packet base state; loaded from configs/pilot-manifest.json so it can never drift.
frozen-pilot-base.known_limitation: Its SAY policy has no required effects, so a zero-effect valid action always exists and first-shot validity does not discriminate repair strategies (observed 2026-08-28).

signal-repair.description: Harbor signal-restoration state with no trivially valid action: both action types require preconditions and required effects, and neither permits a quest-stage effect.
signal-repair.defect: Design defect found on execution: npc_knowledge listed only captain_mira, so any used_fact declared by the acting actor raised NPC_KNOWLEDGE_VIOLATION, a guided-irreparable code that co-occurred in every case and masked the repairable errors. Retained for the record; superseded by signal-repair-v2.

signal-repair-v2.description: Corrected signal-restoration state: the acting actor now has a knowledge set, so a plausible wrong answer lands in the guided-repairable class instead of co-occurring with an irreparable knowledge violation.
